author: Herd_Bull
notes_extra: 168gr Berger VLD Hunting. Shot from 66.0 to 70.0 gr in 0.5 gr steps. 0.02 jump. Remington BDL stainless. Never-fired Norma cases. No chronograph.

author: Herd_Bull
notes_extra: 168gr Berger VLD Hunting. He reshot a 3-shot string of each charge in this span. He loaded six of the 68.5 gr charge and shot two strings. The 68.0 and 69.5 gr groups were best. On Jun 17 he said 69.5 gr had a very minor bolt stiffness.

author: AckleymanII
notes_extra: He did not name the bullet. The thread is 168 gr Berger VLD Hunting. The bullet liked firm contact with the lands.

author: Shooter264
notes_extra: 168 Vlds. He said they work great on elk. Filed as VLD Hunting because the post is about elk. Shot in a couple of 7mm Rem mags. Velocity runs between 3080 and 3100.

author: trailrider121
notes_extra: Berger 168 VLD Hunting. 24 in Criterion. Seated .010 off. Letters F, G, and H, 58.0, 58.4, and 58.8 gr, shared a point of impact and were under MOA. He said he would work around 58.0 to 58.8 gr. Filed as VLD Hunting because he named the hunting bullet.

author: trailrider121
notes_extra: Berger 168 vld hunting. Savage, 24 in. He said this is the charge he is currently using. The thread is an F-class question. Filed as VLD Hunting because he named the hunting bullet. The October 2012 post is the earlier node that includes 58.4 gr.

author: trailrider121
notes_extra: 168s. Upper-end node around 63 to 63.5 gr. He did not test it further. Same Savage 24 in barrel as the H4350 hunting load. Filed as VLD Hunting because the same post names the 168 vld hunting bullet.
